text: Unit-Level Adversarial Tests

The adversarial tests assume honest infrastructure and exercise the decision functions, the proof verifier, the digest function of the audit ledger and the contract at unit level. The adversary, whether an outside requester or a participant of the consent, tries to obtain or keep access without satisfying a condition of C, or to alter the anchored consent or the recorded evidence of a decision. It can supply crafted inputs to the decision functions, alter the bits of a Groth16 proof or its public signals, and send transactions to the contract from an account that is not its owner. Several capabilities are outside the scope of this evaluation, because the prototype does not defend against them. The interface authenticates no role, and each guardian signing key is derived from the public guardian DID. The adversary is also assumed to have no write access to the stores, apart from rewriting an audit event, and no control of the server clock.

The twelve scenarios A1 to A12 together target every component of C and the contract at least once, and each is an automated unit test that applies the attack directly to the targeted component. A scenario is counted as refused when the targeted predicate fails and the decision is DENY, or when the scope check, the Groth16 prover or verifier, or the contract rejects the input. None of the tests drives the running application, its data store or the Sepolia deployment.

{T18} lists the twelve scenarios with their targeted component, their outcome and the test that implements each of them, and {F43} summarises the same outcome as an evaluation matrix before and after the hardening of 1 October 2026. Before the hardening, three attacks were accepted when the service functions were called directly, namely an approval from a signer outside G (A1), a repeated approval from the same guardian (A3) and an empty request scope (A5). None of the three was reachable through the interface as used in the demonstration of 24 September 2026, so they represent a gap in defence in depth rather than a demonstrated breach of the deployed system. Consequently, the service layer now counts only distinct approvals from members of G and requires a non-empty request within the authorised scope. After this hardening, eleven of the twelve scenarios are refused, and the full suite of 36 tests passes, comprising the 23 functional and regression tests and the 13 adversarial tests. In the twelfth scenario, A11, a rewritten audit event changes its digest, but no component of the prototype compares the digest.

caption: Adversarial evaluation matrix for scenarios A1 to A12 before and after the hardening of 1 October 2026

text: The evaluation has six limitations. First, A12 runs the contract source on an in-memory Ethereum virtual machine, so it does not show the behaviour of the deployed bytecode. Second, the SHA-256 digest of the audit ledger is neither keyed nor chained, so the ledger is not tamper-evident against a party with write access to the store. Third, the signed guardian message covers only the consent identifier, the guardian and the network, so a change of scope, purpose, requester, expiry or jurisdiction after approval is not detected. Fourth, A6 relies on the server clock, A7 on the jurisdiction declared by the requester, and A8 on the revocation flag of the local store. Fifth, the Groth16 result holds under a single-party development trusted setup, with the prover and the verifier on the same server. Sixth, the measurements come from a single container and five transactions, so they are indicative only. In addition, these tests are not a penetration test of the deployed system.
Remaining Work for CA3
RO6 is therefore partially completed through its empirical component for RQ1 to RQ4, and the remaining work for CA3 consists of three parts.

items: **Formal assurance.** The soundness property Decision(C, R, t) = ALLOW ⇒ V~I~ ∧ V~A~ ∧ V~P~ ∧ V~T~ ∧ V~L~ and the lifecycle invariant of Section 10 will be verified by model checking of the state machine or by proof over the predicate definitions. Every property must be either verified or refuted by an explicit counterexample.

**Full performance and scalability study.** The preliminary measurements will be repeated over a larger number of consents, guardians and access requests, and the end-to-end decision latency will be measured under concurrent load.

**Extended adversarial evaluation.** The twelve attack scenarios will be extended to larger sets of positive, negative and adversarial scenarios, and enforcement accuracy will be reported over this extended set.

text: In addition, CA3 will address the prototype limitations that the evaluation has exposed. These include the N-of-N approval rule, the server-derived guardian keys, the unauthenticated requester role, the absence of cryptographic DID resolution and VC validation, the missing lifecycle transition check and the unkeyed and unchained audit digest. The schedule of this work is set out in Section 13.
